title: Towards Human Motion World Models via Executable Behaviour Representations
abstract: arXiv:2604.18064v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Human motion world models should capture motion's intentionality by being executable: adaptable to different actions and capable of assessing motion quality. To achieve this, we introduce a domain-specific language ExAct that represents human motions as underspecified programs that can be compiled to a reward model for zero-shot policy inference. By leveraging the compositional nature of ExAct programs, we combine individual policies into executable behaviour representations. We evaluate the utility of the proposed approach by analysing human motion capture for the tasks of human action segmentation and human action anomaly detection. Our results suggest that the improvement in data efficiency and the capture of intuitive relationships between human actions are better than those of task-specific models.

translated_title: 迈向基于可执行行为表示的人类运动世界模型
translated_abstract: arXiv:2604.18064v2 公告类型：替换  摘要：人类运动世界模型应通过可执行性来捕捉运动的意向性：即适应不同动作并评估运动质量的能力。为实现这一目标，我们引入了一种领域特定语言ExAct，它将人类运动表示为未完全指定的程序，这些程序可编译为奖励模型，用于零样本策略推断。通过利用ExAct程序的组合性质，我们将个体策略结合成可执行的行为表示。我们通过分析人类动作捕捉数据，评估了所提方法在人类动作分割和人类动作异常检测任务中的实用性。结果表明，在数据效率提升和捕捉人类动作间直观关系方面，该方法优于任务特定模型。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于领域特定语言ExAct的可执行行为表示方法，将人类运动转化为可编译为奖励模型的程序，从而在动作分割和异常检测任务中实现更好的数据效率和动作关系捕捉。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an executable behavior representation based on a domain-specific language ExAct, which compiles human motions into reward models for zero-shot policy inference, achieving superior data efficiency and intuitive action relationship capture in segmentation and anomaly detection tasks.
